body:
## Parent

#121 — spec: Expected-set entry resolves its skill files

## What to build

Validation stops shadowing the Expected-set entry and stops rebuilding the source layout. It builds one list of validation targets that carries entry identity, the resolved skill file path, and the result together, so verdicts and the report cannot misalign and a missing skill file always fails the gate. The codex variant status becomes a pure projection of the enumerated file list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Validation run end-to-end on a fixture produces the expected verdict for each entry state — fully resolved, missing source directory, missing root `SKILL.md`, malformed provenance, and a variant that ships only `agent.toml` — and the report names the file that failed.
- [ ] Validation targets and their results are one list; no parallel arrays or positional pairing remain in the validation module.
- [ ] A variant that ships `agent.toml` and no `SKILL.md` is reported as an informational status derived from the enumerated files, not as a failure and not by re-walking the filesystem.
- [ ] The codex variant status projection no longer scans skill directories and no longer takes the caller's skill list to de-duplicate against.
- [ ] The codex projection stops emitting the placeholder-directory INFO line; that directory state continues to FAIL validation. (Deliberate behavior change — record it in the PR's deliberate-behavior-changes list.)
- [ ] The entry-state matrix tests move to the enumerator's interface (as in the spec's testing decisions); validation keeps the end-to-end verdict and report assertions, with no duplicated matrix.
- [ ] All existing validation tests pass through the whole-pipeline interface.

## Blocked by

- #122 — Expected-set entry resolves its skill files (expand).
title: Validation consumes enumerated skill files; codex status becomes a projection
